checks: The compact set of all supporting-normal and support-face pairs gives a compact whole contact star. A strictly separating normal to any added point outside K has greater value at the apex than at K; passing to the limit puts the added-region limit and P in one exposed face. This proves locality to the entire star and fixes the other cap signs.

A ball about zero inside K generates positive added volumes on both sides of the selected plane near the exterior apex. The normal-cone ray has a finite last parameter because neither selected orientation belongs to the cone. Moving beyond that endpoint creates an exposed face with strictly positive selected sign; compactness localizes the whole face to the desired other signs.

A fixed shallow cap of K is strictly within the matching signature, and the corresponding cap of the filled hull remains there for sufficiently small fills. Its maximum-depth volume is uniformly positive and the fill volume tends to zero, so continuity gives exact removal. The cap misses every plane. The net selected cap change is exactly minus the negative-side fill volume.

The selected section grows by the planar-relative convex hull with the exterior apex; a relative interior ball establishes strict growth also when the section is one-dimensional. The other sections are unchanged as sets. The two-sided Hausdorff inclusion uses the unchanged support in the shaving direction and proves the interior mark persists.

For strictly convex K there exists a suitable P: choose a ray in the selected plane outside its finitely many proper intersection subspaces, and every exposed face at the radial endpoint is the singleton P. Weight monotonicity needs another strictly positive inverse section weight.

The exact JSON diff changes only the final statement and proof paragraphs to include the two-plane hypothesis. With at least two cuts, the sum of the other inverse section measures is strictly positive, so increasing the selected section strictly decreases its normalized inverse weight.

Selecting an initially minimizing index makes the new minimum at most its strictly decreased weight. The class is preserved by fixed volume, unchanged other caps, and coordinatewise nondecreasing cap constraints.

The source uses N≥2 for this consequence. The independent construction and conclusions about volume and sections still apply to a single cut. No same-wave candidate declares this proof as a predecessor.

issues.defect: The stated local-minimum consequence omits an explicit N≥2 restriction. With N=1 the normalized inverse-section objective is identically 1. A Euclidean ball is therefore a local minimum at fixed volume with no cap constraints, but no exposed face can meet another cutting plane.

overlap.comparison: It treats three prescribed planar normals and a strictly convex body with singleton-face localization. The whole-star proof handles arbitrary finite distinct central planes in any d≥2 and allows flat contacts.
